units.label: Client
units.role: External HTTP caller (curl, browser, or another service) posting orders.

units.label: FastAPI app
units.role: The application process; routes, dependencies, and the BackgroundTasks queue.

units.label: Postgres
units.role: Primary data store for the orders table and the schema migrations table.

units.label: SMTP relay
units.role: External mail relay that accepts receipt POSTs and delivers the email.

flows.title: Customer creates an order
flows.name: Customer creates an order
flows.tagline: POST /v1/orders → row inserted → receipt task enqueued.
flows.narration: An external client POSTs an order to the FastAPI app, which inserts a row into Postgres and queues a background task before returning 201.

steps.narration: The client sends a POST with the order body. The FastAPI router matches /v1/orders and binds the request body to the OrderIn model.

steps.payload: INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount_cents, currency, status, created_at) VALUES (...)
steps.narration: The route calls _insert_order which executes a parameterised INSERT through the async session, then commits.
Postgres acknowledges the commit. The route now holds the generated order id.
The route returns 201 with the order id. The receipt task is queued but has not run yet.

flows.title: Background receipt task fires
flows.name: Background receipt task fires
flows.tagline: BackgroundTasks runs send_receipt() after the response is flushed.
flows.narration: After the 201 leaves the wire, FastAPI's BackgroundTasks runner pops send_receipt, the function loads the order, renders the email, and POSTs it to the SMTP relay.

steps.payload: SELECT id, email, amount_cents, currency, created_at FROM orders WHERE id=:id
steps.narration: send_receipt loads the order row by id so the template has every field it needs.
The task POSTs the rendered HTML to the SMTP relay with a 8-second timeout.
The relay accepts the request and acknowledges with 202. Delivery happens asynchronously on the relay's side.

flows.title: App start applies migrations
flows.name: App start applies migrations
flows.tagline: FastAPI startup event runs Alembic upgrade head before serving traffic.
flows.narration: On boot, the FastAPI startup event runs apply_migrations() which calls alembic upgrade head against the Postgres URL. The app stays out of the gateway until the migration succeeds.

steps.payload: alembic upgrade head (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders, ALTER TABLE ... etc).
steps.narration: The startup event awaits apply_migrations. Inside, Alembic walks the versions folder and applies any unapplied revision against the live database.

steps.payload: alembic_version row at the head revision.
steps.narration: When the head revision matches the database, apply_migrations returns. The startup hook completes and the app begins accepting traffic.

glossary.Idempotency key: A client-supplied token that lets the server detect and reject duplicate requests.
glossary.Background task: A FastAPI feature that runs a coroutine after the response is flushed but inside the same process.

categories.title: Background work
categories.blurb: Receipt task triggered after the response.
